subject: Trial readiness & acceptance gating — open models vs proprietary baseline
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@ledgerly.com>, Chris Malone <chris@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 2, 2026 at 5:22 PM PDT
Subject: Trial readiness & acceptance gating — open models vs proprietary baseline

Hi Elena / Chris —

Thanks again for the demo today — good sync and helpful context on the 3 high-volume intents you want to push to automation. Quick recap of what we discussed and a pragmatic trial plan so your team can evaluate parity vs your proprietary baseline: 

Recap / goals
- Primary goal: determine whether an open model can meet or exceed the baseline on intent accuracy and reduce manual review for the top-3 intents (BillingDispute, RefundFlow, AccountLink).
- Secondary goals: latency SLO (P95), hallucination / factuality headroom, and operational costs (tokens / unit).

Recommended trial plan (2-week pilot)
1) Models to run in parallel:
   - Open candidate A: Llama-3 13B (q4f16) — balanced quality/cost
   - Open candidate B: Mistral-Instruct 7B (q6) — faster, cheaper baseline
   - Proprietary baseline: Ledgerly in-house endpoint (we'll accept your baseline outputs)
2) Evaluation dataset: ~3k labelled examples (you offered a seed set) + live traffic sampling for black-box concordance checks
3) Acceptance thresholds (preliminary — we can tighten):
   - Intent accuracy (macro F1) >= 0.88 vs labelled sample AND no more than 5% degradation vs proprietary baseline on critical intents
   - Reduction in manual review rate: target from current 30% -> <=12% after automation
   - Latency: P95 < 500ms for production routing (hosted); P95 < 700ms ok for dedicated if isolated
   - Hallucination / factuality: human-verified false-positive rate <= 8% on sampled outputs
4) Instrumentation: Redwood will provide an evaluation dashboard (live metrics), example-level diffing, and a prompt set bundle.

Attachments: ledgerly_trial_promptset_v1.csv (seed prompts & labels), redwood_open-vs-prop-cost-estimate.pdf (ballpark token cost for 2-week run).

Next steps
- If you confirm, we can stand up the trial env (hosted/shared) tomorrow and ask procurement for a PO for a short trial credit.
- I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff to agree final acceptance gates and the sample export format. Suggested times: Thu 10:00-11:30 or Fri 09:00-11:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@ledgerly.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Malone <chris@ledgerly.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Trial readiness & acceptance gating — open models vs proprietary baseline

Karthik,

Thanks — this looks good and aligned to what we need. A few clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

1) Data isolation: for the 2-week pilot, can you confirm data retention policy and whether we can use a VPC/private instance? We need logs retained for 90 days and an option to purge after the pilot.
2) Metrics: can the dashboard show per-intent breakdowns and a confusion matrix so our QA team can triage common failure modes?
3) Cost: can you provide an estimated token cost range for the two open candidates for our procurement review? We need a rough number for a 100k token run.

I've attached our seed sample file (ledgerly_test_sample.csv) — it's a 600-row export with typical user channels mixed (chat & email).

If the answers look good, we can start the pilot the week of Jun 8. Procurement: my lead will be looped once we have the cost estimate.

Elena
Elena Ruiz
Product Operations, Ledgerly

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@ledgerly.com>, Chris Malone <chris@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 3, 2026 at 11:08 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Trial readiness & acceptance gating — open models vs proprietary baseline

Elena — great questions, answered below. Also added a short playbook so procurement has the numbers.

1) Data isolation / retention- Redwood hosted: per pilot we can enable a customer data retention policy set to 90 days and run in a soft VPC mode (request-level isolation). If you need full VPC/Private deployment for the pilot we'll engage the Private onboarding (adds ~3 business days). We will include purge API calls and provide an audit log export at the end of the trial.

2) Metrics / dashboard- Yes: the dashboard will show per-intent precision/recall, confusion matrices, top failure examples, and a live concordance panel comparing open model output vs your supplied baseline. We'll share edit access to a dedicated folder in the Drive link below.

3) Cost estimates (approx. for 100k tokens consumption)- Llama-3 13B (q4f16): $90–$140
- Mistral-Instruct 7B (q6): $35–$65
- Note: proprietary baseline cost not estimated; we only compare outcome metrics.

Instrumentation / evaluation plan summary- We propose two evaluation buckets: (A) labelled-sample validation (your 600-row seed + 2.4k pulled from historical dataset) and (B) live A/B shadowing on 10% of traffic with manual review sampling. We'll run both and capture: intent F1, manual-review rate, P95 latency, and a hallucination spot-check.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleBenchmarkLink (I uploaded a quick benchmark template and a short README).

Kickoff slots: Fri Jun 5 at 10:00 PT — does that work for your team?

If yes, I'll ask Marissa to send the trial SOW and a one-sheet on compliance posture (SOC2 summary) for procurement.

—Karthik

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 4, 2026 at 08:07 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Trial readiness & acceptance gating — internal note

Internal — quick ops note before kickoff:

- Suggest we add an adversarial prompt pack (20 examples) targeted at the three intents to stress-test hallucination and slot-filling. We should instrument a "truthfulness rate" metric (human-verified) and set a soft gate >= 0.88.
- Also recommend we enable continuous batching at low latency (we can limit batch windows to preserve P95) to reduce cost during the trial.
- I'll prepare a small eval harness that computes pairwise diffs against the proprietary baseline and surfaces examples where open models disagree but are correct according to labels. That will help the customer feel confident about parity claims.

I'll share the harness before the kickoff so Marissa / Karthik can demo the dashboard.

—Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

This plan looks actionable and aligns with our timelines. We can start the pilot on Jun 9. A few final asks from procurement/security:

- Our procurement lead is Maya Singh (maya.s@ledgerly.com) — I'll loop her once we have the SOW.

Thanks — looking forward.

Elena
